outcome: Fetal cardiac active thyroid hormone (T3) concentration
Phosphorylated insulin receptor substrate 1 (Ser789) abundance in fetal heart
Glucose transporter 4 abundance in fetal heart
Oxidative phosphorylation complexes (I, III, IV) protein abundance in fetal heart
cohort: Female baboons (Papio hamadryas) were randomly assigned to either a control diet or a high fat-high energy diet (~9 months preconception), and their fetuses (6 female, 6 male in each group) were studied at 165 days gestational age.
finding: Maternal consumption of a high fat-high energy diet decreased active cardiac thyroid hormone (T3) and markers of insulin-mediated glucose uptake, while increasing oxidative phosphorylation complexes and mitochondrial abundance in the non-human primate fetal heart.
